title: On Welcoming the stranger at the gate
subtitle: 互助关爱 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 互助关爱（社会服务与人际沟通·互助与关爱）
meta: 主题语境：互助关爱（社会服务与人际沟通·互助与关爱）　|　核心词汇：welcome　|　正文 348 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 welcome 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1968 the ranger ① welcomed the stranger at the gate year after year, and every villager in the valley said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three seasons on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the ranger ② welcomes the stranger at the gate for the whole place without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ welcome the stranger at the gate at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ welcomed the stranger at the gate before — a line in the survey for October 1962 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Welcoming the stranger at the gate year after year, the ranger said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the staff at the far ridge, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ welcome any help offered freely for the whole place, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Welcome any help offered freely at once and never mention it again.

By 1975 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the survey, and a new villager from the next valley ⑧ welcomes any help offered freely year after year every season without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the ridge, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ welcomed the stranger at the gate again when nobody else would.

⑩ To welcome the stranger at the gate, my mother said in 1980, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the valley remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the valley forgets, somebody welcomes the stranger at the gate for the whole place again and somebody must welcome the stranger at the gate year after year all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 欢迎（一般过去式 welcomed the stranger at the gate：1968 年守林人头一回这样做，年年地）
B. v. 欢迎（一般现在 welcomes the stranger at the gate：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 欢迎（不定式 to welcome the stranger at the gate：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 欢迎（过去完成时 had welcomed the stranger at the gate：1962 年十月的踏勘记录上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 欢迎（动名词 welcoming the stranger at the gate 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 欣然接受（welcome any help offered freely：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去欣然接受对手边任何帮助都欣然领受）
G. v. 欣然接受（welcome any help offered freely：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 欢迎（后段两处：新来的村民照例 welcomes any help offered freely，而母亲又一次 welcomed the stranger at the gate）

answers.why: welcome 意为“欢迎”，1968 年守林人年年地欢迎在门口欢迎那位生人，那是山谷里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 welcomed。
welcome 意为“欢迎”，自那以后守林人替所有人把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 welcomes。
welcome 意为“欢迎”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯欢迎在门口欢迎那位生人”，此处为不定式 to welcome the stranger at the gate。
welcome 意为“欢迎”，踏勘记录里 十月 那行字说明早在 1975 年之前就有人欢迎过，故用过去完成时 had welcomed。
welcome 意为“欢迎”，守林人说“欢迎在门口欢迎那位生人这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 welcoming the stranger at the gate 作主语。
welcome 意为“欣然接受”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去欣然接受对手边任何帮助都欣然领受”，should ever 之后用原形 welcome any help offered freely。
welcome 意为“欣然接受”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻欣然接受对手边任何帮助都欣然领受（welcome any help offered freely at once），以后再也不要提起。
welcome 意为“欢迎”，新来的村民每个季节都照例欣然接受对手边任何帮助都欣然领受，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 welcomes。
welcome 意为“欢迎”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次年年地欢迎在门口欢迎那位生人，用一般过去式 welcomed 叙述。
welcome 意为“欢迎”，结尾那句是母亲 1980 年的话：要欢迎在门口欢迎那位生人，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和山谷记住的那一件。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用

多年以后，守林人仍替所有人做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（welcomes the stranger at the gate）

守林人说过，年年地欢迎在门口欢迎那位生人这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（welcoming the stranger at the gate 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻欣然接受对手边任何帮助都欣然领受，以后再也不要提起。（welcome any help offered freely，祈使句）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 welcome 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1968 the ranger welcomed the stranger at the gate year after year, and nobody in the valley forgot it.
Even now the ranger welcomes the stranger at the gate for the whole place whenever the valley asks.
Welcoming the stranger at the gate year after year, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever welcome any help offered freely for the whole place, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new villager from the next valley welcomes any help offered freely year after year every season, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother welcomed the stranger at the gate again, and the valley remembered that half.
